settings.heading: How much should I feed my dog?
settings.row_content:
Feeding amounts depend on factors like age, weight, activity, and the food you use. Here’s a practical starting point:

  • Check the dog food packaging: Most brands include a feeding chart by weight and age. Use that as your baseline.
  • For puppies: usually 3–4 meals per day; follow package guidelines and adjust as they grow.
  • For adults: use the daily amount on the label, split into 1–2 meals.
  • For seniors or very active dogs: adjust portions to maintain a healthy body condition.

Tips:

  • Weigh your dog monthly and adjust to keep a healthy body condition (you should be able to feel ribs but not see them).
  • If you’re unsure, ask your vet for a personalized target (calories per day) based on breed, age, weight, and activity.
  • Monitor energy, coat quality, and stool; significant changes may indicate over- or underfeeding.

If you tell me your dog’s weight, age, breed, and the specific food you use, I can give a more precise starting amount.

settings.heading: Can I feed my puppy bones and treats?
settings.row_content:
Short answer: yes, but with strict safety. Many bones and treats are not safe for puppies.

Key points

  • Avoid cooked, hard, or small brittle bones; they can break teeth or cause choking and GI injury.
  • Only use vet-approved guidance for bones; large, uncooked bones are risky and not always advised.
  • Choose puppy-specific dental chews or large, safe-to-chew toys; supervise every session.
  • Check ingredients for allergens; limit treat amounts to fit daily calories.

Tips

  • Size matters: ensure chews are large enough to not swallow whole.
  • Watch for GI upset and wear; rotate chew types.
  • When in doubt, ask your veterinarian for breed/age/weight–specific advice. If you share those details, I can tailor options and a plan.

settings.heading: How often should I feed my dog?
settings.row_content:
How often to feed depends on age and lifestyle:

  • Puppies: 3–4 meals per day until about 4–6 months.
  • Adult dogs: 1–2 meals per day (many do well with 2; some thrive on once daily if portioned well).
  • Senior dogs: typically 1–2 meals, depending on energy and health.

Tips:

  • Keep a consistent schedule to aid digestion.
  • Measure portions to avoid overfeeding.
  • If you switch foods, transition gradually over 5–7 days.
  • Adjust frequency if your dog has GI issues or weight changes.

If you share your dog’s weight, age, breed, and current food, I can tailor a precise feeding plan.
